why: The oldest Púca Notes APK every OTA bundle built from this tree can run on. It only ever goes UP. Raise it to the release that first ships the new capability whenever a change adds a native plugin, a Capacitor package or an Android permission that the web layer will call, and re-record 'surface' below in the same change (scripts/notes-native-min.mjs fails vitest, build-notes-app.mjs and check-lite-identity.mjs until the two agree). The build writes it into the bundle's version.json, encrypt-bundle.mjs --notes copies it into the .native-min sidecar, and dual-ship.sh mobile-notes publishes it as the manifest's native.min on EVERY release, refusing to lower what a host already serves. 0.9.816: the first OTA-capable Notes APK, and the release that gives the Notes app its own native plugins (NotesNativePlugin, NotesLocationPlugin), @capacitor/filesystem, and the reminder, location, storage and battery permissions they use. 0.9.817: voice notes — RECORD_AUDIO + MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS, which the WebView's recorder needs, and NotesNativePlugin.transcribePcm, which writes a recording down with Android's on-device recogniser or refuses. 'latest' is the newest Púca Notes APK whose NATIVE layer changed, and it is what the OTA manifest's native.version nudges for ("A new Púca Notes app (X) is available"). It used to be the release number, so every release told every installed app it was out of date. The build writes it into version.json as nativeLatest, encrypt-bundle.mjs --notes copies it into the .native-latest sidecar, and dual-ship.sh mobile-notes publishes it as native.version. It is sealed to a fingerprint of the native layer ('latestFingerprint'): change anything the APK's native half is built from and vitest, build-notes-app.mjs and check-lite-identity.mjs fail until you run node scripts/notes-native-min.mjs --record-latest <the release that first ships the new APK>. 0.9.827: KeyboardPlan, NotesKeyboard and NotesNativePlugin (MacroDroid's intent opens a note with the keyboard up).
